info.name: TailorSync Measurement Engine
info.description:
API collection for the TailorSync body measurement backend.

**Endpoints:**
- `POST /api/v1/scan/submit` — AI-guided scan (SMPL mesh + MediaPipe landmarks)
- `POST /api/v1/scan/manual` — Manual 32-field entry (SCAN-09)
- `GET  /api/v1/scan/validation-rules` — Client-side validation rules
- `GET  /api/v1/scan/health` — Pipeline health
- `GET  /health` — App liveness

**Measurement sources (in priority order):**
1. `smpl_anthro_full` — SMPL-Anthropometry with body-part segmentation (best accuracy)
2. `smpl_anthro_trimesh` — Trimesh plane intersection fallback
3. `smpl_mesh` — Direct mesh geometry (width, depth)
4. `landmark` — MediaPipe joint geometry
5. `height_ratio` — Anthropometric proportions × height (last resort)
6. `manual` — Customer-entered value

**Height resolution (priority order):**
1. `height_cm` user-provided → source `user_input` (HIGH)
2. `camera_metadata` sensor fusion → source `sensor_fusion` (MEDIUM)
3. Population mean 170 cm → source `population_mean` (LOW)

variable.description: Base URL of the TailorSync Measurement Engine

request.description: Basic liveness check for the FastAPI application.

Detailed pipeline health. Reports whether the pose model and SMPL model (REAL mode = 6890-vertex mesh with shape blend shapes) are loaded.

When `smpl_model: true` and the server log shows `REAL mode — 6890 verts` the engine is running the full SMPL-Anthropometry pipeline.

item.name: Submit Scan — Minimum (Front only, height provided)

request.description:
Minimum viable submission: user-provided height + one FRONT frame.

All 32 measurements are returned. Key circumferences (chest, waist, hips, neck, bicep, thigh, calf, ankle, wrist) come from SMPL-Anthropometry FULL mode (`smpl_anthro_full`) when the SMPL_NEUTRAL_clean.pkl is present. Lengths and widths come from landmark geometry.

The `validation` block in the response indicates whether the result is ready to place an order (`can_order: true`) or needs a rescan.

Replace `<BASE64_JPEG_OR_PNG_HERE>` with a real base64-encoded image.

response.name: 400 Bad Request — Missing FRONT frame

request.description:
Full 7-pose submission for maximum measurement accuracy.

**Pose sequence:**
- `front` — 0°, facing camera, arms slightly away from sides
- `quarter_left` — 45° turn left
- `side_left` — 90° left profile
- `three_quarter` — 135° turn
- `back` — 180° facing away
- `side_right` — 270° right profile
- `arms_out` — T-pose (arms extended, used for sleeve length M19)

**`client_scan_id`** is a UUID generated on-device at scan start (SCAN-10). Used for idempotency — re-submitting the same `client_scan_id` returns the cached result.

The engine internally keeps the best-scored frame per pose (SCAN-06: top-3 for FRONT/SIDE_L/ARMS_OUT, top-1 for others).

item.name: Submit Scan — Auto Height, Front Only

request.description:
Automatic height estimation via phone sensor fusion — no `height_cm` required.

- `camera_height_cm` — distance from floor to phone camera lens (user places phone on a surface)
- `tilt_angle_deg` — downward camera pitch from horizontal (from device accelerometer)
- `focal_length_px` — optional; defaults to a 65° vertical FOV if omitted

All measurements are capped at MEDIUM confidence. Response includes `height_source: "sensor_fusion"`.

item.name: Submit Scan — Auto Height, Minimal (no focal_length_px)

request.description: Sensor fusion without focal length. The server assumes 65° vertical FOV — slightly less accurate (±5–8 cm vs ±3–5 cm) but still MEDIUM-confidence. Use this when the app cannot read focal length from EXIF.

SCAN-09: Customer enters all measurements by tape measure.

All supplied fields are:
- Flagged `is_manual_override: true`
- Set to MEDIUM confidence (human measurement error ±1–2 cm is expected)
- Set to source `manual`

Missing fields default to `null` with LOW confidence. Use for customers who prefer tape-measure input, or to override specific LOW-confidence scan results.

Only `height_cm` is required. All M-code fields are optional.

request.description:
Returns all validation rules as a JSON object so the Flutter app can run the same checks client-side before submitting a manual entry form.

**Response sections:**
- `field_ranges` — absolute physiological min/max per M-code (e.g. chest: 50–200 cm)
- `population_norms` — ANSUR II height-relative mean/SD ratios + Z-score thresholds
- `cross_rules` — ordered list of cross-measurement consistency rules (e.g. waist < chest)
- `version` — changes when rules are updated; Flutter should re-fetch on version mismatch

Fetch once per app launch and cache locally.

response.name: 200 OK — Validation Rules
